And these things of God's glory are thrown behind, and if all nations are as nothing and are not considered, to what likeness have you likened him? For what will be the image of him, and what will be equal in weight or nature or glory? Is it by the crafts of a builder or the skills of a woodworker? Or is it as if formed into an image towards something of the creations? That is, was a human-like statue made? By no means. For nothing can be equal to him. For God, being by nature and not being another, will surpass all things. Having spoken, then, beyond all that is made and called into being, he ridicules the making of idols and says that an unrotting wood is chosen by a builder, and wisely seeks how he will set up an image of it so that it will not be shaken. So, it would be the work of the builder's skill to fashion a god according to their opinion, with the greatest safety, so that it will not be shaken and broken when it falls. Therefore, the worshipers of idols were in error, with no skill of building on the earth. But not even the handmade things would be saved if the craftsman had not wisely sought the means by which they could stand and have an unshaken foundation. Someone might say, and very reasonably, through the voice of David: 'The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the work of human hands.'

All who do and trust in such things are like them, having ridiculed the construction of idols, and turning the discourse to shame and correction of the erring, and showing them the fault in this matter, saying: You do not know? You do not hear? From the beginning it was not announced to you? You do not know the foundations of the earth? The foundations of the earth are its last and furthest parts. You have known, he says, those from the ends to the ends. You have heard, and it was announced to you from the beginning. But what was announced? That God, the one by nature and truly, is one and only; wood and stones, and nothing else, are made into gods by humans. For the God-inspired Scripture has not been silent. The knowledge of truth has been proclaimed from above, through patriarchs, through the law and prophets. For when the only-begotten Word of God became human and appeared to those on earth, then for the first time the deception of error occurred. But the accusation of idolatry was ancient, as I said.
pass_b_english: The things of God's glory are cast aside, and the nations are considered as nothing. If all nations are as nothing, to what likeness can God be compared? What image can be made of him, and what can be equal to him in weight, nature, or glory? Can it be through the crafts of a builder or the skills of a woodworker? Or is it as if formed into an image towards something of the creations? That is, was a human-like statue made? By no means, for nothing can be equal to God. God, being by nature and not being another, will surpass all things.

The worshipers of idols are in error, with no skill of building on the earth. But not even the handmade things would be saved if the craftsman had not wisely sought the means by which they could stand and have an unshaken foundation. As David says, 'The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the work of human hands' (Psalm 115:4).

All who engage in such practices and trust in them are like those who ridicule the construction of idols. By turning the discourse to shame and correction, the erring are shown the fault in this matter, and without excuse, the fault in this matter is revealed to them, saying: Do you not know? Do you not hear? Has it not been announced to you from the beginning? Do you not know the foundations of the earth, which are its last and furthest parts? Those who are from the ends to the ends have known, and they have heard, and it was announced to them from the beginning.

But what was announced? That God, the one by nature and truly, is one and only. In contrast, wood and stones, and nothing else, are made into gods by humans. The God-inspired Scripture has not been silent on this matter. The knowledge of truth has been proclaimed from above, through patriarchs, through the law and prophets. This proclamation occurred even before the only-begotten Word of God became human and appeared to those on earth, an event that marked the beginning of the deception of error. However, the accusation of idolatry was ancient, a fact that underscores the long history of this error.
